question: Successive discount of 30%, 20% and 15% are equivalent to a single discount of:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **successive discount formula**: Net Discount = a + b − (a × b)/100

Combine **30%** and **20%**: 30 + 20 − (30 × 20)/100 = 50 − 6 = **44%**

Combine **44%** and **15%**: 44 + 15 − (44 × 15)/100 = 59 − 6.6 = **52.4%**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three successive discounts of **30%**, **20%**, and **15%**.

**Formula:** Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51ffcb4a5e86019ec0bd7d6b481c2ca61c389494d3dcaf68ac6011501a2fffd0.png] 

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** = 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount (30%) = 100 × (70/100) = 70

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount (20%) = 70 × (80/100) = 56

⇒ Price after 3rd discount (15%) = 56 × (85/100) = 47.6

⇒ **Total Discount** = MP − Final SP = 100 − 47.6 = 52.4

⇒ **Equivalent Discount Percentage** = (52.4 / 100) × 100 = 52.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

The formula x + y + (xy/100) can be used for any successive changes. For discounts, use negative values for x and y.

Effective Multiplier Method

The equivalent discount is 1 − [(1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100)].

Marked Price vs Selling Price

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless otherwise stated. SP = MP − Discount.</p
